races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)

runners_data.name: I Ready
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 6f Good trip last time out (OR 82, highest in field), jockey Dylan Browne McMonagle retains the ride, and the prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Shesthedevil; the recent record shows 1W1P in similar going conditions.

runners_data.name: Banks Of The Boyne
runners_data.note: Consecutive placed efforts at 7f and 6f Good suggest consistent form with pace, Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is a bonus at the weights, and the prominent style allows Banks Of The Boyne to race right off Shesthedevil's quarters without being exposed early.

runners_data.name: Shesthedevil
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, she has a course-and-distance win on Good to her name and Jack Kearney (3) keeps the ride; the key risk is whether an uncontested lead at 6f proves a platform to quicken or allows rivals to simply hunt her down late.

runners_data.name: High Morals
runners_data.note: Has placed at 8f Good and shown early speed, but a pronounced tendency to fade in the final stages is a serious concern at this trip; Chris Hayes is a significant jockey booking, though that alone cannot offset the closing weakness flagged repeatedly in her form.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes over for J P Murtagh's yard which posted 3 winners from 25 runners in the last 14 days; all form has come at 5f and stepping to 6f is an unproven query, while a hold-up style in a race likely to be run at a controlled pace makes it hard to generate momentum.

runners_data.name: Away And Gone
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's runner has 46 days between runs and a tongue-tie fitted, both of which add uncertainty; all three runs have come at 5f or 6f Good, but the hold-up style and absence of a placing on Good ground make this a wait-and-see profile.

runners_data.name: Howlin Wolf
runners_data.note: Three runs all at 5f or 6f on Good, finishing 4th-7th-7th, suggesting consistent mediocrity rather than an improving curve; the hold-up style in a race with a controlled pace gives James Ryan limited options to find daylight late.

runners_data.name: Alrashdeyah
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a major jockey booking for what is by far the lowest-rated horse in his current string; however, she has finished last or near-last in her two most recent starts, carries a finish-fade flag, and her true hold-up profile means she is unlikely to be where the map places her, limiting her realistic chance in this shape.

runners_data.name: Mr Montauk
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's yard recorded 6 winners from 50 runners in the past 14 days and Mr Montauk was placed twice at 6f Good — the most relevant course-and-distance form in the hold-up group; though a natural closer bumped forward by the race shape, Declan McDonogh may find enough space if the pace softens late.

races.paceDynamic: Shesthedevil is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to dispute the lead, she should stride to the front early and control the tempo through the first two furlongs of this 6f Curragh nursery on good ground. I Ready and Banks Of The Boyne are the natural stalking types most likely to sit just off her shoulder and apply the first sustained challenge around the two-furlong pole. High Morals has shown early speed but a tendency to fade late, meaning she will likely press up prominently without being a true pace rival to Shesthedevil. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable gallop — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel in behind and pounce in the final furlong, rather than true hold-up horses making late ground from the rear. Alrashdeyah and Mr Montauk are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to a midfield map position because the field holds more come-from-behind horses than the diagram can place at the back; I Ready and Banks Of The Boyne are the prominent runners most likely to actually secure their natural position directly behind the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shesthedevil Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Shesthedevil leads uncontested and sets a fair but manageable pace, the race becomes a test for the closest pursuers.
scenarios.body: Shesthedevil dictates from the off without pressure, reaching the furlong marker on her own terms, and the nearest prominent horses pounce as the pace lifts late on the Good ground. This shape is the most probable outcome and rewards horses who travel sweetly in second or third throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Shesthedevil Outstays Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Shesthedevil's uncontested lead results in a true front-running tour de force where no chaser gets to her.
scenarios.body: Having stolen a tactical advantage with zero pace pressure, Shesthedevil quickens again in the final furlong before the prominent horses can organise their challenge, and her previous course win on Good ground supports her ability to hold on. This scenario demands she reproduces her best form, but her recent profile and unchallenged lead give it genuine weight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Shesthedevil goes too hard early and the prominent horses get swallowed up, gifting late runners a run through.
scenarios.body: An overly-strong early pace drains the principals, and hold-up horses threading through tired rivals in the final 100 yards become live contenders — though this scenario is constrained by the fact that Mr Montauk and Alrashdeyah are not ideally placed to execute it from their likely forward positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Wide Optics
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stop-start and the race degenerates into a flat, bunched finish with no clear sectional shape.
scenarios.body: Without a true run-to-pattern race, horses who simply stay on steadily through the field can emerge, but the absence of proven stayers in this 2-year-old 6f field makes this the least likely shape. Celestial Crown and Away And Gone, stepping up from 5f, could theoretically benefit from a messy, attritional finish.

watchPoints.text: Shesthedevil (Kearney) — watch whether she leads by more than two lengths entering the final quarter-mile; if she does, it signals a potential front-running score and all race shapes shift around her.

I Ready (Browne McMonagle) — the highest-rated runner with a recent win over course and distance needs to be prominent from the gate; if she gets shuffled back early she loses her primary tactical advantage.

High Morals (Hayes) — watch for her dropping back sharply inside the final furlong as she has done before; a repeat fade would suggest the prominent position flatters her and should be noted for future races.

Mr Montauk (McDonogh) — O'Brien yard in form and McDonogh is a strong front-against-pace jockey; watch whether he uses his redistribution position to push forward aggressively rather than settle back, which could change the complexion of the race.

Alrashdeyah (Murphy) — Murphy's high-profile booking on the lowest-rated runner is the market watch point of this race; if punters pile in despite the form figures, it warrants monitoring whether connections have a specific angle the formbook does not show.

races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden
Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap

runners_data.name: Bundle Of Interest
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for McCreery and Dylan Browne McMonagle, wearing a visor; has finished third on comparable Good ground and the 8f trip suits, but needs a proper pace injection that this race shape is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Neo Smart
runners_data.note: Bolger-trained five-year-old with a prominent profile that fits the map position perfectly here; uncontested lead on Good ground over a mile is a significant tactical gift, though trainer has had no winners from five runners in the past 14 days.

runners_data.name: Kitty Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Andrew Slattery with the 7lb claimer Orla Tynan aboard; won over 8f on Good ground previously and brings solid course-distance form, though 19 days between runs and recent poor finishing positions are concerns.

runners_data.name: Tofino
runners_data.note: Cromwell's 4-year-old has Good-ground form at this trip and placed most recently over 8f on Soft, suggesting versatility; Gary Carroll takes the mount and the horse's ability to travel prominently if needed is an asset in a steady-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Marambo
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Chris Timmons who wears a hood; sim-going record at this trip is thin (1 from 4) but the prominent profile is naturally well-suited to tailing Neo Smart, and James Ryan can place him handily on the inner.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature — has won off fast-run races and finished second on Good ground — but the congested rear means McGuinness's veteran is mapped to midfield, a position that masks its true style; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Pallatine Hills
runners_data.note: True hold-up type for Eddie & Patrick Harty who wears a hood; recent form shows a run of 5s and 6s in 8f-9f Good-ground handicaps and sim-going figures are modest — squeezed into midfield on the map but naturally operates from the back.

runners_data.name: Sherekiya
runners_data.note: Style unknown for the three-year-old from Dermot Weld's yard; Hayes takes the ride and the horse has placed once in four runs on Good ground, with form figures of 7-4-5-7 suggesting mid-division finishes rather than a strong late burst.

runners_data.name: Lamberella
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Marnane who carries a "fades in finish" flag — a serious concern in a race where the pace is steady and there is little room to generate momentum from the rear; 36 days since last run adds mild freshness doubt.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old with a genuine hold-up profile and two course wins on Good over 7f-8f; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim helps at the weights, but the horse's natural position at the back will be crowded and the STYLE_FIT note limits realistic expectation.

runners_data.name: Avec Grand Plaisir
runners_data.note: Fahey's three-year-old has placed at 8f on Good ground and Ronan Whelan is a positive booking; a hold-up type who may find the congested rear frustrating, and the limited sim-going strike rate (0 wins from 3 comparable) keeps expectations measured.

runners_data.name: Sancerre Rock
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery and returning after 65 days off — that layoff is notable in a competitive handicap; a hold-up type who wears a tongue-tie and hood, and has yet to win on Good ground, with all four recorded runs on it producing mid-field finishes.

runners_data.name: Ella's Gold
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Matthew Smith's yard with a habit of placing (0W/1P from 5 on sim-going) but wears a pari-mutuel hood; a natural hold-up horse whose best form came on Soft, and the Good ground at Curragh is an unresolved question.

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Martin Hassett's 4-year-old carries a "fades in finish" flag and sits at the foot of the weights with a low OR of 56; sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 5) and the style redistribution from true hold-up to midfield makes this a long shot.

runners_data.name: Alto Sax
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's 5-year-old wears blinkers and has a broad distance profile — won at 10f on Good, runs here at 8f; the hold-up style pushed to midfield, and the apprentice claimer Reese Holohan's 7lb allowance is the principal tactical lever available.

runners_data.name: Cannonball Queen
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 46) for S M Duffy, with a "fades in finish" warning and form figures of 15-14-12 in recent handicaps suggesting consistent tail-ender finishes; mapped to midfield from a true hold-up base, and the STYLE_FIT penalty is well-earned.

races.paceDynamic: Neo Smart is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner handicap and, crucially, faces no meaningful early pressure — with the entire remainder of the field profiled as hold-up or prominent types, Neo Smart can control tempo from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over Curragh's flat mile. That uncontested lead on Good ground is a significant tactical advantage; a steady-to-moderate pace is the near-certain outcome, compressing the field and reducing the time available for hold-up horses to generate meaningful momentum in the straight. The field is saturated with hold-up types — Sancerre Rock, Pallatine Hills, Ella's Gold, Comfort Line, Dinamine, Alto Sax, Navajo Point and Cannonball Queen are all genuine rear-of-field horses who have been mapped into midfield positions they are unlikely to physically occupy, meaning the back of the race will be heavily congested and finishing runs will be curtailed. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently just off Neo Smart's unhurried pace and pounce from a position of coverage, rather than those who need a truly strung-out gallop to deliver their best effort from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Neo Smart Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Neo Smart is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured pace that suits a prominent racer striking at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Neo Smart controls every yard at a tempo of its own choosing, and a horse sitting second or third with cover lands a decisive blow as the pack struggles to close from a congested rear; the Good ground and flat track remove any stamina test that might expose a pace-setter.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Neo Smart at close range, conserves energy through the steady early pace, and quickens decisively in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With the pace honest but not fierce, a prominent tracker who travels well within themselves has first run on the field and covers ground efficiently on the flat Curragh straight; the hold-up brigade, stuck in a traffic jam at the rear, cannot close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If pace quickens sharply inside the final quarter-mile and creates enough separation to allow a hold-up horse to find a clear passage on the outside.
scenarios.body: A genuine closer with class or a course-form angle — such as Bundle Of Interest or Dinamine — finds a gap on the wide outside as the field fans out, benefiting from a late surge that briefly rewards deeper horses; this remains a minority scenario given the field's rear-end congestion and moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Market Movers
scenarios.trigger: If a false start, interference, or unexpected early surge from multiple horses disrupts Neo Smart's rhythm and forces a contested lead.
scenarios.body: A ragged early pace would string the field out and benefit a horse who handles pressure and has adaptable tactics; this is a low-probability outcome given the clear dominance of hold-up types who have no incentive to race prominently.

watchPoints.text: Neo Smart (Declan McDonogh) has a clean lead with zero pace rivals — if allowed to dictate unchallenged at a dawdle, watch whether the field realises too late to close and Neo Smart simply outkicks a flat-footed pack up the straight.

The rear of the field — Dinamine, Sancerre Rock, Ella's Gold, Alto Sax and Cannonball Queen — will all be seeking the same ground at the same moment; watch for significant traffic problems and interference entering the final two furlongs.

Lamberella and Navajo Point both carry "fades in finish" flags in a race where a slow pace will compress the field — both are at real risk of being swallowed up at the death even if travelling well at halfway.

Sancerre Rock returns after 65 days off for trainer-jockey Andrew Slattery — watch for signs of ring-rustiness early and monitor whether the market drifts or firms significantly before the off as an indicator of stable confidence.

Marambo (James Ryan) is the one prominent-profile horse positioned naturally to stalk Neo Smart — watch where Ryan slots him in the first two furlongs, as a position directly behind the leader could prove the race's key tactical moment.

races.name: Velo 'Official Coffee At The Curragh' Irish EBF Maiden
Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap

runners_data.name: Sonoran
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for G M Lyons who has placed twice in five runs on Good ground at around this trip; 36 days off but trainer runs at 15% over 14 days and Gary Carroll is a booking worth noting — needs a clear run from off the pace but the race shape is squarely in his favour.

runners_data.name: Thyer
runners_data.note: Has two wins and six places from 15 runs on Good ground — the standout surface record in this field; hold-up style suits the projected honest tempo but a 5-year-old on a mark of 76 with a 0/4 trainer strike rate in the last 14 days is a concern, and Leigh Roche will need to find daylight in a congested straight.

runners_data.name: Youcansaythatagain
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good for A Oliver last time out and has the most relevant recent form in the race; sits prominent which is ideal tracking the front pair, and Ben Coen's 2/10 14-day trainer record suggests the yard is in decent touch — a 3-year-old with only two runs but the profile fits a contested honest gallop.

runners_data.name: Great Mover
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for W McCreery; trainer at 3/18 in 14 days and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride — but recent form (663260) is modest and the horse has gone 0 wins from 8 attempts on Good ground, suggesting this pace role may see him weaken when Admiral Will Brown pushes on.

runners_data.name: Unterberg
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Laura Hourigan who won over 12f on Standard in latest win; recent Good-ground form is poor (14th at Curragh over 12f last time) and the 7-year-old needs to rediscover something here — Oisin Murphy's presence is the most significant positive but the form trajectory is troubling.

runners_data.name: Admiral Will Brown
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won over 10f on Good on his most recent victory; 3-year-old carrying only 131lbs with 3lb claimer Wesley Joyce aboard — the pace duel with Great Mover is the defining tactical question and if the battle costs him, he will be vulnerable from 2f out.

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 3-year-old for Jack Foley, placed over 9f on Good but without a win in five; amateur jockey Orla Tynan (7lb claimer) could struggle in heavy prominent traffic with five horses looking for that position, and the step to 10f is untried.

runners_data.name: Mighty Danu
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Gavin Cromwell — trainer at 3/20 in 14 days and Jack Kearney claims 3lb; won over 7f on Good but this is a significant step up to 10f having been off 38 days, and the blinkers first applied could sharpen him or cause issues in traffic.

runners_data.name: Storzando
runners_data.note: Style is uncertain — the one unknown in the race; three runs only, all on Good ground, and Michael Mulvany's yard has had no winners in 14 days from 14 runners; Declan McDonogh takes the ride which adds tactical intelligence but the lack of form data makes this hard to place in any scenario with confidence.

runners_data.name: Blackjack Hills
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who carries the hood; won twice at a mile on easier surfaces and is 0 from 1 on Good over 12f — this Good 10f trip is an unknown quantity but the drop from 80 OR to 65 is significant and Matthew Smith's yard is quiet (0/1 in 14 days); one for the each-way market at the price if the pace plays to the closers.

runners_data.name: Guinelot
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good last time for K J Condon (1/7 in 14 days) and wears a hood — a progressive 3-year-old who is prominent in style and has the most directly relevant course-and-distance form; Shane Foley is a high-quality booking and this horse is at the right end of the market if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: 6-year-old for Paul Flynn who ran just 4 days ago — freshness is an immediate concern and the trainer has no winners from 21 runners in the last 14 days; prominent in style with a hood and has two wins on Good ground over slightly shorter trips, but this quick turnaround and cold trainer form suggest this is one to oppose.

races.paceDynamic: Admiral Will Brown and Great Mover are both confirmed front-runners over this 1m2f trip at the Curragh, and with five of twelve runners wanting prominent positions, the early exchanges are unlikely to be sedate — an honest, competitive gallop is the base expectation. Admiral Will Brown (Wesley Joyce, a 3-year-old claiming 3lb) won over 10f on Good last time and will press hard for the lead, while Great Mover shapes as a genuine pace rival who may not cede willingly; their duel could stretch the field through the first half-mile. The prominent cluster — Youcansaythatagain, Unterberg, Liberation Date, and Guinelot — will be jostling for position around the 2-3f-out danger zone, creating significant traffic risk for any horse without a clear run. This contested, honest tempo sets up best for hold-up horses with the ability to pick through the field in the straight, particularly those with proven Good-ground form at this sort of trip — Sonoran, Thyer, and Mighty Danu profile as the chief beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest pace, closers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Admiral Will Brown and Great Mover sustain their duel and set a genuine gallop that softens the prominent pack turning for home.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners push each other through the early stages and the prominent traffic around 2-3f out creates gaps that open late; hold-up horses with Good-ground form get first run on the outside in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, prominent lands
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other out quickly and a prominent type steals a march mid-race before the closers organise.
scenarios.body: A runner sitting just behind the early scrimmage — tracking the pace without being embroiled in it — times the move perfectly as the field concertinas turning in; the straight is run at a reduced tempo that suits the horse already in front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner grinds it out
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace setters establishes early dominance unchallenged and the other concedes, allowing a controlled solo lead.
scenarios.body: Admiral Will Brown, if Great Mover is restrained or falters early, could dictate a measured gallop that plays to stamina and rail position; at 1m2f on Good ground this is achievable for a horse who won over 10f last time out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow early, late sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the field crawls through the early stages before a sprint finish develops.
scenarios.body: A bunched field hitting the straight together turns the race into a furlong dash; horses with the best turn of foot and a clean position rather than hold-up types would thrive, making the outcome unpredictable but favouring sharp prominent runners.

watchPoints.text: Admiral Will Brown and Great Mover must be watched closely at the break — if both race hard for the lead the gallop will be genuine and will compromise both, but if one drops off immediately the other gains a free rail advantage that changes the complexion of the entire race.

Traffic congestion between 2f and 3f out is the key danger for hold-up horses Sonoran, Thyer, and Mighty Danu — with five runners wanting prominent positions, the pocket risk is acute and jockeys will need to move early or be trapped in a wall.

Nibras Rainbow ran just four days ago and must be monitored for signs of tiredness from the 5f mark onwards — if the pace is honest this horse could capitulate quickly and cause interference for hold-up types attempting to thread through late.

Unterberg's Curragh form is poor despite the Oisin Murphy booking — watch whether he travels fluently in the early stages or begins to struggle for position, as a 14th-place run last time over the same course signals a horse not firing at the moment.

Storzando's unknown style is worth watching from the start — Declan McDonogh will quickly establish whether this horse wants to go prominent or settle, and that decision in the first furlong will determine which scenario becomes most likely.

races.name: Newbridge Silverware Royal Whip Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for JP O'Brien with Declan McDonogh aboard; ran well to win over 7f on Good last time but stepping up sharply to 1m2f today, and from the back of this small field against a sole front-runner this trip extension may arrive a furlong too late structurally.

runners_data.name: Omni Man
runners_data.note: JP O'Brien's second string here, and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride off 10 days' rest; his natural game is racing prominently but with Rebel Ascendant and A Boy Named Susie ahead of him in the pecking order he is unlikely to secure his preferred berth, making a clean run harder to engineer.

runners_data.name: A Boy Named Susie
runners_data.note: Top-class jockey Oisin Murphy is a significant booking for Donnacha/Aidan O'Brien's 3yo; has placed five times in a row including two seconds at 1m2f on Good ground, making the trip and going combination a clear fit — the 43-day absence is the only question mark worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Charles Fort
runners_data.note: Long-absent (328 days) AP O'Brien 3yo who profiles as a pure front-runner stepping well up in trip from sprint distances in his form string; sets the entire race shape and benefits enormously from having no pace rival, but stamina for 1m2f on return from such a layoff is a genuine query.

runners_data.name: Rebel Ascendant
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner in the field (OR 120) with Jack Davison's yard sporting zero winners in five outings over 14 days; only two runs on record but won over this exact trip on Soft, and 97 days fresh with the blinkers noted — if class tells on reappearance this is the form pick of the prominent stalkers.

races.paceDynamic: Charles Fort is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to pressure him — he should stride to the front from the gates and control tempo on his own terms over the 1m2f trip at Curragh on Good ground. Rebel Ascendant, A Boy Named Susie, and Omni Man are all prominent-style horses who will look to track close to the pace, though with three runners sharing that role, at least one will be shuffled wider or deeper than ideal. The field holds more prominent-hunting types than the map can accommodate: of those, Rebel Ascendant (highest OR, freshest to this trip) and A Boy Named Susie (Grade-quality jockey in Murphy, strong place record) are most likely to secure the coveted stalking spot just off Charles Fort. With a single front-runner setting a moderate, uncontested tempo, this race shape strongly favours a well-positioned prominent stalker who can strike from a prime tracking position when Charles Fort is collared in the straight — hold-up types are structurally disadvantaged by the likely lack of pace pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stalker Pounces Off Honest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Charles Fort dictates a fair but unforced gallop and a prominent tracker times their run to perfection from just off his quarters.
scenarios.body: Charles Fort controls from the front without being harried, meaning the pace is genuine but not ruinous; the horse sitting second or third wheel has a perfect slingshot into the Curragh straight with cover throughout the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Charles Fort steals enough margin from a slow or passive field that the prominent chasers cannot close the gap.
scenarios.body: With no pace rival to interrupt his rhythm, Charles Fort coasts into the straight with a lead that proves too large to reel in over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns surprisingly strong early and the field strings out, leaving hold-up horses with an unimpeded late run.
scenarios.body: Cowardofthecounty, racing from the back, benefits if the fractions are high enough to cause attrition among the front contingent; Omni Man, though a natural prominent type operating out of role here, could also pick up pieces if the pace burns.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, No Pattern
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses battle for position early and disrupt Charles Fort's rhythm, turning the race into a rough-and-tumble affair.
scenarios.body: The 3-1 weight advantage for the 3yo prominent runners could create early jostling for the rail, bunching the field and producing an unpredictable straight; Rebel Ascendant's freshness (97 days off, handicap-topweight) makes him capable of flourishing in a scramble if it suits.

watchPoints.text: Charles Fort sets the pace unchallenged — watch whether Wayne Lordan settles him on a true or false gallop, as the entire race hinges on that tempo judgement given the 328-day absence.

Rebel Ascendant and A Boy Named Susie will both want to sit directly off Charles Fort's quarters — watch the first two furlongs for position jostling between Murphy and James Ryan that could compromise one or both runners early.

Omni Man is a natural prominent type who cannot get his preferred position in this shape; watch whether McMonagle elects to push forward regardless or accepts a deeper role, as either choice carries a tactical cost.

A Boy Named Susie's 43-day absence is mild but worth monitoring in the paddock — five consecutive placed efforts suggest peak fitness, but a first run for Oisin Murphy under this yard could reveal whether the booking signals a big run is expected.

Going is confirmed Good throughout the card at Curragh with no sectional variation across the two 1m2f races — no ground-related concerns for any runner, and the surface should ride consistently true to the forecast pace shape.

races.name: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Grayrobin
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 5f wins on Good at Curragh give this runner strong course-and-distance form; Chris Hayes knows the track well, and 23 days since last run is a comfortable return — a natural prominent racer who should find a handy berth without the worst of the scrimmage.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for the in-form Joseph O'Brien yard (6/50 T14); form figures of 1-3-0-3-7 show inconsistency and that 0 and 7 in similar going are notable concerns — prominent style should secure a position but the form profile raises questions about reliability under pressure.

runners_data.name: April Mist
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners a filly with a smart 2nd at 5f on Good at Curragh last time; her natural racing style is prominent, but with five rivals chasing the same positions she is likely to race further back than ideal — her STYLE_FIT of 0.80 tempers confidence, though the Lyons yard has been ticking over (2/13 T14).

runners_data.name: Armor Supreme
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner; Rossa Ryan takes over for Diego Dias after a 60-day break, and that layoff is worth noting on a horse with only three runs — all three came on Good going and produced 9-2-1, so the improvement trajectory is clear if the freshness translates positively.

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is an extreme quick turnaround and the most pressing concern here; Ben Coen rides a horse whose true style is prominent but who, squeezed out by a field saturated with pace, will likely find itself further back than it wants — a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 is scant consolation when the body is asked to back up so fast.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Diva
runners_data.note: Diego Lima partners a stablemate of Armor Supreme for Diego Dias; the recent form run of 6-2-1 shows she can win but the 6 and 5 in 6f races suggest 5f is her trip — a prominent runner who should secure a decent position in the chasing pack but faces stiff class opposition from OR=95 and OR=120 rivals.

runners_data.name: Concorde Landed
runners_data.note: OR=120 makes him comfortably the highest-rated runner in the field alongside The Baddie; Wayne Lordan rides a horse who won on debut at 5f Good and was a fair 4th on his second start — only two runs limits certainty but the class ceiling here is substantial, and a prominent style suits this race shape directly.

runners_data.name: New Bond Street
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over for the Twomey yard (same trainer as Concorde Landed) on a horse that has posted three consecutive placed efforts at 6f — the step down to 5f is unproven, and his natural prominent style is displaced into a midfield slot by the overcrowded pace picture, making his task harder than his OR suggests.

runners_data.name: Stellar Path
runners_data.note: Shane Foley cannot disguise a form string of 9-8-8-9 — this runner has finished last or near-last in every recent start and is flagged for fading in the finish; the tongue-strap is noted but the OR=57 is a significant gulf below the class of the field, and a hold-up style in a race that may not truly stop is a poor fit.

runners_data.name: The Baddie
runners_data.note: Complete unknown — no form string, no listed days since last run, UNKNOWN going profile — trained by Diego Dias who saddles two other runners today, giving the yard useful race intelligence; Gavin Ryan's booking is a positive signal, but lightly-raced uncertainty means this runner is impossible to place confidently within any scenario despite carrying the joint-highest OR=120.

races.paceDynamic: Armor Supreme is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one genuine pace-setter in a 10-runner field, should secure the lead uncontested from the outset and dictate a sustainable, measured gallop over this flat Curragh 5f. Behind him, a congested bank of prominent types — Grayrobin, Star Prospect, Concorde Landed, Brazilian Diva and April Mist — will jostle for the four or five positions immediately behind the leader, creating a scrimmage 2-3 furlongs out that threatens to trap or unsettle runners who need a clear passage. The field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions; Concorde Landed and Grayrobin, on class and recent winning form respectively, are best placed to actually land the prominent slots, while New Bond Street and Arrowstock — true prominent types pushed into a midfield mapping — are unlikely to achieve their natural position and face a compromised trip. A sustainable pace with early positional chaos behind the leader strongly favours horses who can either secure a handy berth without scrimmaging or who possess the class to quicken through a compressed mid-race pack — the prominent-to-lead profile with a sharp turn of foot is the winning archetype here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Armor Supreme Controls, Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Armor Supreme dictates an uncontested, measured pace and his rivals fail to close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Armor Supreme settles into his own rhythm unchallenged and, on Good turf which suits him (3/3 on sim-going), has enough in reserve to repel challengers; Concorde Landed, tracking close on a retrieval mission from stall, is the most likely danger coming with a smooth run from a handy position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group quickens collectively in the final 2f and overhauls Armor Supreme before the line.
scenarios.body: The jostling behind the leader resolves into a multi-horse surge at the 2f pole, where Concorde Landed's superior OR=120 gives him the class edge to punch through; Grayrobin, who has won twice at 5f on Good at this track, is ideally positioned to benefit from the compressed finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage causes interference 2-3 out and briefly opens a lane for a hold-up horse to arrive late.
scenarios.body: April Mist, a natural prominent type shuffled wide by redistribution, could find space if the pack ties itself in knots; The Baddie, an unknown quantity from Diego Dias (who also trains Armor Supreme and Brazilian Diva), carries genuine lightly-raced intrigue and could emerge if the race falls apart in front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfielders Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Armor Supreme sets a fraction too strong early and fades, leaving redistributed midfielders to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: New Bond Street and Arrowstock, genuine prominent types forced into a midfield role, would need the pace to collapse entirely for their late runs to materialise — an unlikely shape given Good ground and a single, self-regulating leader.

watchPoints.text: Armor Supreme's 60-day layoff is the single biggest risk to the dominant scenario — watch his pre-race demeanour and whether Rossa Ryan is instructed to bounce him immediately, as any sluggish break could allow Concorde Landed or Grayrobin to steal the rail and flip the race shape entirely.

The prominent congestion between Grayrobin, Star Prospect, Concorde Landed and Brazilian Diva is likely to produce bumping or checking 2-3 furlongs out — any runner caught in the squeeze at that point, especially those already racing out of role, risks a severely compromised chance.

Arrowstock running just two days after its last start is a welfare and performance flag — watch for signs of fatigue in the final furlong, and note that Ben Coen may ride conservatively to protect the horse, which could cause interference if rival jockeys expect him to press forward.

The Baddie's complete absence of public form makes it a live dark horse for any scenario — Diego Dias saddling three runners today means connections have significant information; monitor market moves in the final 20 minutes before post time.

New Bond Street stepping from 6f to 5f for Oisin Murphy is worth tracking as a pace dynamic factor — if Murphy pushes forward aggressively to reclaim the natural prominent position the horse is denied in the mapping, it intensifies the early scrimmage and increases the probability of Scenario C.

runners_data.name: Mary Shoelaces
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact 5f Good-ground combination and has two wins from her similar-going record of 10 runs; hold-up by nature but has shown the ability to deliver a clean late run, and the 7lb claim from Jessica O'Gorman is a meaningful weight relief on a 142lb allotment.

runners_data.name: Soulful Diva
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose sole win came over 5f on Good ground and who has decent place form at this level; Nathan Crosse keeps the ride and, while her hold-up style means she needs a gap to appear, her 5f course form gives her a legitimate live chance.

runners_data.name: Arctic Steps
runners_data.note: Has won twice over 5f on Good and shown consistent placed form at the trip, with Dylan Browne McMonagle an obvious upgrade in the saddle; a natural hold-up runner whose best work at this course and distance suggests he can deliver a clean finish if given daylight.

runners_data.name: Bold Optimist
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with the most extensive similar-going record in the field (12 runs) and a recent second over 5f Good; Ben Coen is a key booking and, although the horse races from the back, it has the profile of a durable handicapper who can find the frame at a course it knows well.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent racer aside from the leader and therefore the best-placed horse to track Ballysax Lil' Mick throughout; eight-year-old with 13 runs on Good ground at this track but limited recent form, and Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim helps offset his OR of 69.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: Trainer W McCreery in excellent form (3/18 in 14 days) and the horse has a strong record at 5f on Good ground with two wins from seven similar-going runs; a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield position by field congestion, so style compromise is the central caveat — STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflects that.

runners_data.name: Surpass And Shine
runners_data.note: Won once over 5f on Good ground and has course form, but recent runs have been poor (9100-0 latest), and Seamie Heffernan inherits a horse that is genuinely a closer forced to race closer than ideal by the crowded back-end of this field; STYLE_FIT tag at 0.93 tempers claims.

runners_data.name: Kiss Don't Tell
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago, which is the sharpest fitness concern in the field; a prominent-profile three-year-old for McLoughlin but with no wins from four runs and a best of second on Tapeta — the quick reappearance and lack of turf wins make this one hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Carries a fades-in-finish flag alongside the lowest OR in the competitive portion of the field (56) and has recorded a string of double-digit finishes recently; dropped from 8f and 7f to 5f but still showing no form, and the redistribution into midfield only adds to the complexity — very hard to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Ballysax Lil' Mick
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and therefore guaranteed an uncontested lead; OR of just 48 and a record showing mostly mid-field or worse finishes when the pace gets serious, but the tactical advantage of a lone lead on flat Good ground at the Curragh is real and should not be underestimated.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: Dropping sharply in trip — all four runs on record are at 7f to 10f, making this a speculative 5f debut; a genuine hold-up type displaced into midfield by field congestion and rated only 47, so both the trip compression and the positional compromise work against it.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.note: Carries a fades-in-finish flag, ran two days ago, and is rated only 48; won over 6f on Soft but Good-ground 5f turf form is thin and the McLoughlin yard has sent out two runners in two days which warrants monitoring, though the STYLE_FIT displacement into midfield further complicates matters.

races.paceDynamic: Ballysax Lil' Mick is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 5f handicap and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, should dictate an honest but uncontested gallop on Good ground at the Curragh. Harry's Hill is the only genuine prominent racer mapped to that position, and he will track Ballysax Lil' Mick's sectionals from close range, but the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, meaning the leader should not be burned up early. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Surpass And Shine, Happy Henry, Heart Of Eternity, Pure Valour and Lady Landhort are all true closers redistributed into midfield because of overcrowding at the back, and only the sharpest of those is likely to find clear daylight in time; Happy Henry and Surpass And Shine are best placed to secure a workable midfield pitch given their course and trip profiles. With a controlled, sustainable pace set by one lone leader on a flat, fair track, this race shape heavily favours horses who can travel prominently in the first two or three, get a clean passage racing off the rail, and produce a sustained finishing effort — the prominent and strong-finishing midfield profile is the one to side with, not the deep hold-up brigade who face a traffic problem from the outset.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Ballysax Lil' Mick secures the rail uncontested and the chasing pack fails to close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Ballysax Lil' Mick sets a measured, unforced gallop and, with no rival pushing it for position, conserves enough energy to find a second gear at the furlong pole; the prominent closers who track it need to quicken on cue but a fair pace on Good ground may simply not set up enough of a late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pack tracks closely throughout and the prominent hold-up types get clean runs to reel in the leader inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Horses like Mary Shoelaces and Arctic Steps, who have genuine 5f Good-ground form and can travel in the first half of the field, pick up the pace once Ballysax Lil' Mick's advantage narrows; Good ground rewards those with a true, sustained finish rather than an explosive burst, suiting this profile well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race and the redistributed hold-up horses find gaps sooner than expected.
scenarios.body: Happy Henry and Surpass And Shine, forced to race closer than ideal but still with room to manoeuvre, could benefit if the early fractions prove more generous than anticipated and the leader ties up; their Good-ground course records give them residual claims, though the style compromise marked by their STYLE_FIT tags caps confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so slow that it becomes a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, creating a bunched cavalry charge.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling pace would theoretically benefit deep closers, but with most genuine hold-up types already displaced into midfield and carrying STYLE_FIT discounts, the advantage is marginal; Soulful Diva, who won last time on Good ground at 5f, has the turn of foot to cope with a sprint-finish scenario if she threads a gap.

watchPoints.text: Ballysax Lil' Mick is the sole front-runner — watch whether Wesley Joyce settles it conservatively or kicks on from the gate, as the fractions it sets will dictate every other scenario in this race.

Harry's Hill is the only genuine prominent horse and therefore has a clean, unobstructed route throughout; if it travels sweetly just off Ballysax Lil' Mick through the first three furlongs, it is best placed of all to challenge in the final furlong.

Mary Shoelaces and Arctic Steps both have strong 5f Good-ground winning form and capable jockeys — watch their positions jumping from the stalls, as either being drawn wide or missing the break could strand them in the congested hold-up pack.

Kiss Don't Tell and Lady Landhort both ran two days ago; monitor their paddock behaviour and early movement — horses returning that quickly to Good turf at the Curragh can run flat if the quick turnaround has not suited them.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Happy Henry, Surpass And Shine, Pure Valour, Heart Of Eternity, Lady Landhort) will all be competing for the same limited space in the middle to rear of the field — watch for traffic trouble from the two-furlong pole, particularly if the pace compresses the field.
